Maya (docs): quick heads-up — I opened a docs PR to consolidate the Python/TS/Go streaming + pagination snippets into a single sandboxed example set. goal: fewer copy/paste bugs and clearer retry guidance. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4021
Sam (eng): awesome. does the PR change the cursor TTL guidance? that's bitten a couple teams (we saw regressions when cursors got GC'd early)
Maya (docs): yes — I added an explicit note about cursor TTL and an example that shows renewing cursors before pagination resumes. also added a tiny warning about mixing prefix caching with resume tokens.
Leo (sdk): nice. can you show the Go snippet you want to replace? last time we had two different cursor examples (one used a channel per page, the other used a single streaming loop) and folks got confused.
Maya (docs): current draft replaces both with a single pattern: streaming loop that writes pages to a local temp buffer, then yields page tokens. snippet (py):
```python
# keep a rolling cursor, renew before next request
with client.stream_chat(model="open-llm/fast", session_id=session_id) as s:
    for event in s:
        if event.type == "message":
            buffer.append(event.text)
        elif event.type == "cursor_expiring":
            client.renew_cursor(session_id=session_id)
```
Maya (docs): and the TS/Go examples follow the same high-level flow — avoid storing cursor tokens as the single source of truth without a short-lived lock.
Anya (qa): found a flaky in the py snippet tests — the test harness times out if the streaming mock doesn't send a final `end_of_stream` event. we should explicitly show the `close()` or finalization step in all examples.
Sam (eng): good catch. also callout: retries + pagination. If you get an intermittent 502 mid-page, we should show how to resume with `cursor_resume` and use exponential backoff. tiny pseudo snippet for backoff: 
```js
// TS pseudo
let attempt = 0
while (attempt < 5) {
  try {
    await client.fetchPage(cursor)
    break
  } catch (e) {
    attempt++
    await sleep(2 ** attempt * 100)
  }
}
```
Leo (sdk): for the Go SDK, please use the new `StreamIterator` API (we deprecated the old `NextChunk` in v0.8). I'll add a small helper in the sdk repo that mirrors the py `with` pattern. linking SDK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/178
Maya (docs): thanks — I'll update the doc to reference SDK v0.8+ and add a short migration note. also adding a note to not rely on absolute request counts for pagination; use the server-provided cursor when available.

Maya (docs): ok, will add a one-line sentence and a small code comment about jitter — thanks.
Sam (eng): one more: the console screenshots in the PR show token-cost breakdown; those are great but can we blur the API keys and replace with `REDACTED` placeholder? legal asked for that.
